paper_metadata.title: Comparative Performance Analysis of Quantum Machine Learning Architectures for Credit Card Fraud Detection

experiments.description: Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) evaluated on the BankSim credit card fraud dataset across three feature maps and four ansatz choices, using a simulator-based Qiskit workflow.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical fraud features are encoded through quantum feature maps (Pauli, ZZ, Z) into a 4-qubit circuit.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize cross-entropy loss for binary fraud classification.

problem_instance.description: Binary credit card fraud classification on the BankSim dataset after balancing with random undersampling.

dataset_specification.description: BankSim agent-based bank payment simulator; 594,643 original records over 180 simulation steps, reduced to a balanced subset of 492 fraud and 492 non-fraud transactions; features include Step, Customer, ZipCodeOrigin, Merchant, ZipMerchant, Age, Gender, Category, Amount; train/test split 80/20; MinMaxScaler applied to scale features to [0,1].

data_preprocessing_details: Random under sampling to balance classes to 492 fraud and 492 non-fraud samples
Conversion of Age categorical values to integers using regular expressions
Numerical encoding of categorical features Customer, Gender, Merchant, and Category
Removal of ZipCodeOrigin and ZipMerchant due to lack of variability
Conversion of remaining features to numerical values
MinMaxScaler normalization to [0,1]
80/20 train-test split
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Performance evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and loss; results reported for multiple feature map/ansatz combinations.

classical_postprocessing: Metric computation (accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, loss)

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: mostly stabilizing with some zigzag/oscillatory convergence depending on configuration

speedup_claims.caveats: Paper states no demonstrated quantum speedup; complexity discussion indicates same asymptotic class as classical simulation for the studied circuits.
